clue.text: Captain playing well in match

blocks.note: on a cricket scorecard (c) marks the captain
a player on form is playing well

explanation.surface: A skipper is having a good game in an important fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captain' tempts CO or CAPT; here it is the single letter C used in cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply or be in agreement with something, which is what matching means here.

clue.text: Teach wrongly about male cat

indicators.note: done wrongly means done out of order, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the shuffled letters surround the other piece

blocks.note: the letters of teach, rearranged
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Giving a tomcat the wrong lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a big cat of the African savanna, the fastest land animal.

clue.text: Name one German river

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
I is the Roman numeral one
Ger is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Asking someone to name a single river in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a German river; the river is in West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is the principal river of West Africa, flowing through Mali, Niger and Nigeria.

clue.text: Herb used by Lear's daughter stuffing two ducks

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside something, so this name sits within the other pieces

blocks.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O; two of them
Regan is one of King Lear's three daughters

explanation.surface: A cook seasons the stuffing for a pair of ducks with a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' looks like culinary stuffing, which fits a herb nicely, but it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb of the mint family, much used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Conventional place for white lines?

blocks.note: first meaning: moderate, avoiding extremes
second meaning, literal: the centre of a highway, where the painted markings run

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second meaning as a literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road describes views or tastes that are moderate and mainstream, which is what conventional means.

clue.text: Stop after snake makes for pitch

indicators.note: 'after' places the stopping word behind the reptile word in the answer

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: Coming to a halt after spotting a snake on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is a tarry substance, and asphalt is a bituminous material of the same kind used for surfacing roads.

clue.text: Floor covering in a church beneath cross — note part damaged round end of aisle

indicators.note: in a down answer, beneath means placed after the piece above it
something damaged is broken up, so its letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter, here the one taken from aisle
round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the last piece

blocks.note: taken as written
X is a cross
a minster is a large church
C is a musical note
the letters of part, rearranged
the last letter of aisle

explanation.surface: A church carpet beneath a cross, with a note that part of it is worn near the end of the aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: Axminster is a Devon town famous for its woven carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: An Axminster carpet is a machine-woven pile carpet, named after the Devon town, used to cover floors.

clue.text: Criticise a revolutionary's swagger

blocks.note: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly
taken as written
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary; the 's joins him to what follows

explanation.surface: Finding fault with a rebel's arrogant strut.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence of style, close in sense to swagger.

clue.text: St Michael converted one trying to find the elixir of life

definitions.text: one trying to find the elixir of life

indicators.note: something converted is changed into another form, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A saint has converted a seeker after eternal life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' fits the religious surface of St Michael, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval alchemists sought the philosopher's stone and an elixir granting eternal life, as well as transmuting metals into gold.

clue.text: Climber to catch up on exercise, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the words, not their spelling

blocks.note: to tend is to attend to or catch up on a task, and drill is exercise

explanation.surface: A mountaineer needs to make up for missed training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a plant part.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the slender coiling shoot by which a climbing plant attaches itself, so it does the climbing.

clue.text: Bird dog needing no lead

indicators.note: a lead is the front, so going without it means losing the first letter

blocks.note: a beagle is a hunting dog

explanation.surface: A well-trained dog that can be walked without a leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a dog's leash; cryptically it is the leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Sister in party dress is able to

blocks.note: a do is a party
a mini is a short dress
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A woman wears a party dress because she can.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dominican is a nun of the Order of Preachers, and a nun is addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Sailor, man wearing oilskin hat

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
a man's name
someone wearing a coat is in it

explanation.surface: A seaman dressed in a waterproof hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a container with the man inside the hat, but the pieces simply run in order, wearing giving IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin was a sailor's tarred or waterproofed hat, as well as the waterproof sheet the word now usually means.

clue.text: Plainly caught by king

indicators.note: 'by' sets the catching letter beside the monarch, the two pieces joining up

blocks.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A batsman obviously out, caught off the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, as in 'loud and clear', clear means distinctly, in a way that is easy to perceive.

clue.text: Husband has quarrel about film of Tube station

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt
on means concerning, about
The Hill is a 1965 Sean Connery film set in a military prison

explanation.surface: A husband argues over which film to watch at the Underground station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' reads as a row, but it is the archaic word for a crossbow bolt. Harrow-on-the-Hill is a station on London's Metropolitan line.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow-on-the-Hill is a London Underground stop, and the Tube is the everyday name for London's Underground railway.

clue.text: Anagram bottom row

blocks.note: the rear is the bottom, the backside
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: An instruction to shuffle the letters of the bottom line of a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'Anagram' is not an instruction but a verb meaning to rearrange letters, and so it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To anagram letters is to put them into a different order, which is what rearranging means.

clue.text: Brief description of a person and his sailing boat?

blocks.note: first meaning: a short written portrait of someone
second meaning, split differently: the ketch belonging to a character, that is a person

explanation.surface: A short profile of a man together with a note about his yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after the S and it reads as a person's ketch, a ketch being a two-masted sailing boat; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A character sketch is a short piece of writing portraying a person's personality.

clue.text: Mimic brings matter to be printed about opening of theatre

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: copy is text for publication
ca, circa, means about
the first letter of theatre

explanation.surface: An impersonator offers material for a newspaper about the start of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat is someone who imitates others, so it means a mimic.

clue.text: Resolute man, social worker

blocks.note: Adam, the first man
an ant is a social insect, and a worker ant is a sterile female

explanation.surface: A determined man employed in social work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a profession; it is an insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unshakeably determined, refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Wise guy corrected on walk round centre of Ely

indicators.note: something corrected is put right, changing its order
round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go outside the selected letter
the centre of a three-letter word is its middle letter, the one taken from Ely

blocks.note: the letters of on walk, rearranged
the middle letter of Ely

explanation.surface: A smart alec is put right while walking round a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is someone who acts as if they know everything, the same as a sarcastic wise guy.

clue.text: Dance floor — see weed coming over?

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming over means sitting on top of the other piece

blocks.note: to hoe is to weed
to floor someone is to knock them down

explanation.surface: A gardener on a dance floor, hoeing weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like a noun, a dance floor, but it is a verb meaning to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance, or a party where such dancing takes place.

clue.text: Father carrying weapon in Italian city

indicators.note: one who is carrying something holds it within, so the parent word goes around

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A dad walking around an Italian city with a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy, famous for its ham and cheese.

clue.text: Complicated? Present in further detail

blocks.note: first meaning: intricate, involved, an adjective
second meaning: to expand on, a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently: the adjective ends in '-it', the verb in '-ate'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means intricate and detailed; as a verb it means to develop or expand on a point.

clue.text: Maxim's in the morning, about ten after ten

indicators.note: about means around, so the morning letters surround the numbers

blocks.note: am is the abbreviation for morning
X is the Roman numeral ten
ten written as 1 and 0, looking like the letters IO, coming after the first ten

explanation.surface: A man called Maxim is up at ten past ten in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten appears twice: once as a Roman X, once as the digits 1 and 0 read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth or accepted principle, which is a maxim.

clue.text: Pal with toucan cut up a melon

indicators.note: something cut up is chopped into pieces and its parts rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend and a tropical bird share a sliced melon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantaloup, more often spelt cantaloupe, is a variety of orange-fleshed melon.

clue.text: Friend in a plane, latest from Mexico

indicators.note: the latest of a word's letters is its final one

blocks.note: taken as written
a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
the last letter of Mexico

explanation.surface: A pal arriving by air, the most recent visitor from Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a friend, borrowed into English as informal slang.

clue.text: Joy and editor taken out

blocks.note: a treat is a source of joy
ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A woman called Joy and the newspaper's editor were taken out to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joy' looks like a woman's name; it is a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To be treated is to be taken out and paid for, as when someone treats you to a meal.

clue.text: A motel demolished at back of Nelson's Column

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
a demolished building is knocked down and its parts lie in a new jumble

blocks.note: taken as written
the possessive 's aside, the last letter of Nelson

explanation.surface: A motel knocked down behind the famous monument in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's Column is the London monument, so 'Column' reads as part of a name; it is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A telamon is a carved male figure used as a supporting pillar in classical architecture.
